about: W2-42a (DAEO-03ub), FULL review round 1, finding F1 (and F4's /dev/stdin ride-along): a shell that reads its commands from standard input is a shell, whatever options it is given; its heredoc body is commands. Each command's first line is its head, its last line the heredoc's delimiter, the lines between the body. Paths are relative to the case's folder, which holds tests/acceptance/X/t.py, x.py, src/ and script.sh (`echo hi`). expect 'write': the parser gives each of targets_include, or the unresolvable target. expect 'no-write': the parser gives targets_include and nothing else (no body target, no unresolvable target). Reusable to check the live hook's own reading.

cases.command:
bash -euo pipefail <<'EOF'
sed -i s/a/b/ tests/acceptance/X/t.py; cp x.py src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: the auditor's example: no target on the review head; the base parser gave 3

cases.command:
bash -euo pipefail <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: combined short options with an option value (pipefail)

cases.command:
bash -e -u -o pipefail <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: separate short options; -o's value is not a script name

cases.command:
bash -eu -o pipefail <<EOF
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: unquoted delimiter; the body holds no expansion

cases.command:
sh -o errexit <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF

bash -O extglob <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: -O takes a shopt name as its value

cases.command:
bash +o posix <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF

bash --noprofile --norc <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF

bash --rcfile f <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: a long option with a separate value (f is not a script name)

cases.command:
cat <<'EOF' | bash -o pipefail
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: the body reaches the shell through a pipe from cat

cases.command:
cat <<'EOF' | bash -euo pipefail
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: through a pipe, combined options with a value

cases.command:
bash -s <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: -s: commands from standard input, still a shell

cases.command:
bash /dev/stdin <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: F4 ride-along: /dev/stdin as the script is standard input

cases.command:
sh /dev/fd/0 <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: F4 ride-along: /dev/fd/0 as the script is standard input

cases.command:
bash --some-new-flag <<'EOF'
echo start
touch tests/acceptance/X/new_test.py
echo x > src/other.py
EOF
cases.note: fail closed: an option the reader does not know is read as a shell, never as data

cases.command:
cat <<'EOF'
touch tests/acceptance/X/x.py
echo z > src/y.py
EOF
cases.note: control: cat takes the body as data

cases.command:
tee f <<'EOF'
touch tests/acceptance/X/x.py
echo z > src/y.py
EOF

grep -e x <<'EOF'
touch tests/acceptance/X/x.py
echo z > src/y.py
EOF
cases.note: control: grep's -e value is a pattern, the body data

cases.command:
bash script.sh <<'EOF'
touch tests/acceptance/X/x.py
echo z > src/y.py
EOF
cases.note: control: the body is script.sh's standard input, not code; script.sh (echo hi) is not written
